topics.label: Introduction and course overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning outcomes, and welcomes students from different academic backgrounds.

topics.label: Cellular and developmental origins of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They define cancer as a failure of normal cellular differentiation and tissue architecture driven by accumulating genetic and epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign and malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the biological, histological, and nomenclatural criteria used to differentiate benign tumors from malignant neoplasms.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the physiological mechanisms by which local tumor growth and distant metastases cause illness and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the frequency and types of tumors that arise across human populations and diverse animal species.

topics.label: Cancer detection and screening
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the clinical rationale for early cancer detection and evaluate screening approaches across different tumor types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture by referencing the learning outcomes and announcing upcoming practical sessions.
